_comment: The sg-child-support subject sidecar. ONE subject, TWO regimes, because they
are two halves of one announcement and they share their nouns: the same child's
date of birth decides a Baby Gift cohort in sg-csp.l4 and a qualifying-child age
band in sg-childcare-leave.l4. Splitting them would duplicate the family.
WHAT MAKES THIS SUBJECT UNUSUAL, and what a reader should know before trusting
any figure it produces: its primary source is an ANNOUNCEMENT, not an enactment.
The SG Child Support Package was announced at the National Day Rally on
23 August 2026 and is to be implemented from 1 April 2027. No Bill has been
introduced and the Child Development Co-Savings Act 2001 is unamended. So the
rule-version axis here does not carry two versions of one statute; it carries
the scheme as administered TODAY against the scheme as ANNOUNCED, and the
encoding says so at every dated figure. See NOTES.md.
'checks.min_dated_arms' is 0 ON PURPOSE, and this is NOT the same claim
sg-succession's 0 makes. That corpus has no rule-version axis at all. This one
has a thoroughly dated axis, but it reaches it through a named predicate --
`the rules in force include` <a named DATE constant> -- rather than through a
line that compares `RULES EFFECTIVE DATE` against a Date LITERAL, which is the
shape p3-check's temporal-closure sub-check matches. The count that check would
report is therefore an artefact of the indirection and not a measure of the
temporal structure. A 0 floor makes the sub-check report NOT CHECKED rather
than vacuously green over an empty matched set. Raising the floor would require
inlining date literals at every call site purely to be counted, which is a worse
encoding; the honest move is the 0 and this paragraph.

'checks.min_assertions' is 79 = the assertions_total that `l4 run --json` reports across the module set, MEASURED 2026-08-25 via etc/go/lib/assert-report.mjs: 71 in sg-child-support-cases.l4 and 8 in sg-csp-openfisca.l4. The four rule modules carry none, by design, because a rule module that asserts about itself is not independent evidence. The floor exists because 'no failed assertion' is satisfied vacuously by an empty results[].

'comparison' declares the fork register only, and deliberately declares NEITHER
'modules' NOR 'surface_map'. SPEC.md section 8's diff oracle compares an
additional encoding against the committed one; there is no prior encoding of
this subject anywhere, so there is nothing to diff. The registers are genuine
P1/P2/P4 deposits regardless, so a deposit-path run validates them and p8-diff
reports SKIPPED with a named reason.

'p7-wizard' is NOT declared. The leg renders a dedicated wizard module and this subject has none: its question-asking surface is the four @export functions in sg-child-support.l4, which the p7-mcp leg covers. Declaring the leg without the module makes subject.mjs refuse the sidecar, which is the check working.

sg-csp-openfisca.l4 is a PROJECTION of sg-csp.l4 into the subset `l4 openfisca` v1 accepts -- no date builtins, no WHERE/LET, entity-and-period formulas. It is in the module list because its eight assertions are the only thing keeping the projection from drifting into a second, undeclared encoding: each one asserts the projection equal to sg-csp.l4 for one cohort band. Its emitted artifact is projections/openfisca/sg_child_support.py.
